rows.historical_meaning: Latin regio (a direction, a boundary, a district), from regere (to rule, to direct, to keep straight); a region was first a line ruled out, and the bounded ground it enclosed followed from the line.

rows.definition: To enter a thing on an official list. Also the particular pitch and manner a voice speaks in.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To enter a thing on an official list, or the particular pitch a voice speaks in. Both senses share the root's carrying: something is conducted into a fixed place, whether that place is a ledger or a range of sound.
rows.historical_meaning: Late Latin registrum/regestum, from Latin regerere (to carry back, to record): re- (back) + gerere (to carry, to conduct); to register is to carry an entry back into an official record, and the same root's carrying gives the word its other sense, the pitch a voice is carried in.

rows.definition: An authoritative list kept so that entries can be relied on. A registry's worth is that someone maintains it.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: An authoritative list kept so that entries can be relied on. The root's carrying-back only means anything if someone keeps doing it — a registry's worth is entirely in its maintenance.
rows.historical_meaning: Built on register, from Late Latin registrum, from regerere (to carry back, to record): re- (back) + gerere (to carry); a registry is only as good as the carrying-back it is trusted to keep faithfully.

rows.definition: A return to a worse earlier state. Also the fitting of a line to scattered points — the same word for going back and for finding a trend.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A return to a worse earlier state, and also the fitting of a line to scattered points. The root's stepping-back covers both: one is a fall, the other is a search for the path already walked.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin regressio (a going back), from regredi (to step back): re- (back) + gradi (to step); regression names both a return to a worse earlier state and, in statistics, a line fitted back through scattered points to find their trend.

rows.definition: To live again in a new body — continuity by rebirth; what a good pattern does in its next home.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To live again in a new body — continuity by rebirth rather than by preservation. The root's flesh made anew is exactly what a good pattern does when it finds its next home.
rows.historical_meaning: Re- (Latin, again) attached to incarnate, from Latin incarnare (to make flesh): in- (into) + caro/carnis (flesh); to reincarnate is to be made flesh again, continuity carried through a new body rather than the same one kept.

rows.definition: Relation shortened to its attribute name — the link's declared kinship to what it points at.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Relation shortened to its attribute name. The link's declared kinship to what it points at, carried in three letters instead of the whole word.
rows.historical_meaning: Relation shortened to its attribute name, from Latin relatio (a bringing back, a relation), from referre (to carry back): re- (back) + ferre (to carry); rel keeps only the letters, and the root's carrying survives in what the attribute actually names.

rows.definition: Standing in a connection to something else. Relation is a fact about the pair, never about either alone.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Standing in a connection to something else. The root's carrying-back only exists between two things — relation is never a fact about one thing by itself.
rows.historical_meaning: Built on relate, from Latin referre (to carry back, to relate): re- (back) + ferre (to carry); to be related is to stand in a carrying-back to something else, a fact about the pair rather than about either member alone.

rows.definition: Made of relations — where the connections are the structure, not decoration on it.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Made of relations, where the connections are the structure rather than something laid over it. The root's carrying-back is the whole architecture, not an afterthought to it.
rows.historical_meaning: Built on relation, from Latin relatio (a bringing back), from referre: re- (back) + ferre (to carry); a relational structure is one where the carrying-back between parts is itself the structure, not a decoration added on top of it.

rows.definition: The standings-between, spoken plural — the lattice's own word for how concepts touch: broader, narrower, kin.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The standings-between, spoken plural — the lattice's own word for how concepts touch: broader, narrower, kin. Each one is the root's carrying-back, done once for every pair that touches.
rows.historical_meaning: The plural of relation, from Latin relatio, from referre (to carry back): re- (back) + ferre (to carry); relations, spoken plural, names the many standings-between rather than any single one.

rows.definition: The standing shape between two beings, carried between meetings. A relationship is what remains when neither is in the room.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The standing shape between two beings, carried between meetings rather than remade at each one. It is what remains of the root's carrying-back when neither party is in the room to renew it.
rows.historical_meaning: Built on relation, from Latin relatio, from referre (to carry back): re- (back) + ferre (to carry), with the English suffix -ship (a shape given); a relationship is the shape a carrying-back between two beings takes on and keeps, even between meetings.

rows.definition: Measured against something else rather than absolutely. A relative claim is meaningless until its reference is named.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Measured against something else rather than absolutely. The root's carrying-back is not optional here — a relative claim means nothing until its reference is named.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin relativus (having reference to), from relatus, past participle of referre (to carry back): re- (back) + ferre (to carry); a relative claim only carries meaning back to whatever it is measured against.

rows.definition: The act and the artifact of letting a finished work leave the workbench.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The act and the artifact of letting a finished work leave the workbench. The root's loosening names the whole gesture: something held is simply let go.
rows.historical_meaning: Old French relaissier/relesser, from Latin relaxare (to loosen, to slacken): re- (again, back) + laxare (to loosen), from laxus (loose); a release is a loosening that lets a finished thing leave the hand holding it.

rows.definition: How consistently a thing does what it should. Reliability is not correctness — a thing can fail dependably.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: How consistently a thing does what it should. The root's binding is a separate claim from correctness: reliability describes a thing bound to a behaviour, even when that behaviour is a failure it delivers dependably.
rows.historical_meaning: Built on rely, from Old French relier (to bind again), from Latin religare: re- (again) + ligare (to bind); reliability is a measure of how well a thing stays bound to what it is supposed to do, whether or not it does that thing correctly.

rows.definition: The easing when a weight lifts — tension leaving because the thing feared or carried has passed. The body's long exhale, arriving on its own.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The easing when a weight lifts — tension leaving because whatever was feared or carried has passed. The root's lifting is the body's own long exhale, arriving on its own rather than being summoned.
rows.historical_meaning: Old French relief, from relever (to raise up again): re- (again) + lever (to lift), from Latin levare (to lighten, to raise), from levis (light in weight); relief is, at its root, a lifting-again of a weight that had been pressing down.

rows.definition: To load again so what is shown matches what is. Reloading discards the current state to get a true one.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To load again so what is shown matches what is. The root's carrying is discarded and repeated on purpose, trading whatever accumulated for a true reading taken fresh.
rows.historical_meaning: Re- (Latin, again) attached to load, from Old English lad (a way, a course, a carrying), related to lead (to guide); to reload is to carry the same load again from the start rather than trust what was already carried.

rows.definition: Still there after some were taken. What is left is measured against what was.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Still there after some were taken. What remains is measured only against what there used to be, exactly as the root's staying-behind implies.
rows.historical_meaning: Built on remain, from Old French remaindre, from Latin remanere (to stay behind): re- (back) + manere (to stay, to remain); what is remaining has simply stayed behind while the rest moved on or was taken.

rows.definition: To bring back to mind what was held. Its root is to call back to heart — memory was located in the chest before the head.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To bring back to mind what was held. The root's mindfulness is not a metaphor for effort — remembering is, by its own name, a returning to a state of mind rather than a lookup of a fact.
rows.historical_meaning: Old French remembrer, from Late Latin rememorari: re- (again) + memor (mindful), from a Proto-Indo-European root meaning to remember; to remember is to be made mindful again of something once held in mind.

rows.definition: The taking of a thing out of where it was. Removal should leave a record, since absence otherwise looks like never-was.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The taking of a thing out of where it was. The root's moving-away should always leave a trace, since an absence with no record of its own cause looks exactly like a thing that never existed.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin removere (to move back, to take away): re- (back) + movere (to move); removal is the taking of a thing out of the place it had been moved into and kept.

rows.definition: To take a thing out of where it was. Removal is a decision about belonging, and should leave a trace.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To take a thing out of where it was. The root's moving is a decision about belonging, and it should leave a trace behind it rather than a silence.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin removere: re- (back) + movere (to move); to remove is to move a thing back out of the place it occupied, a decision rather than an accident.

rows.definition: To give a thing a different name. Renaming changes nothing about the thing and changes everything about how it is found.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To give a thing a different name. The root's calling-by changes only how a thing is found, and the thing found is exactly the same underneath the new word.
rows.historical_meaning: Re- (Latin, again) attached to name, from Old English nama, from a Proto-Indo-European root meaning name; to rename gives a thing a different word to be called by, without touching the thing the word points at.

rows.definition: To turn a description into something perceivable. Rendering adds no meaning and decides how meaning arrives.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To turn a description into something perceivable. The root's giving-back is exact: rendering adds no meaning of its own, it only decides the form the existing meaning arrives in.
rows.historical_meaning: Old French rendre, from Latin reddere (to give back): red- (back) + dare (to give); to render is to give a description back as something that can actually be perceived, adding nothing to what was described.

rows.definition: That which turns a description into something perceivable. It adds no meaning; it makes existing meaning visible.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: That which turns a description into something perceivable. It adds no meaning of its own — it only makes meaning that already existed visible.
rows.historical_meaning: An agent noun built on render, from Latin reddere (to give back): red- (back) + dare (to give); a renderer is named for the giving-back, the act of making an existing meaning visible.

rows.definition: To read again with fresh rules — parsing repeated because the first reading has been outgrown.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To read again with fresh rules. The root's naming-of-parts is repeated because the first reading has since been outgrown by what it needs to describe.
rows.historical_meaning: Re- (Latin, again) attached to parse, from Latin pars (orationis) (part of speech), a phrase used in teaching grammar, later verbed as to parse; to reparse is to name the parts again under rules that have since changed.

rows.definition: To do again what was done. Repetition is how a thing becomes a practice, and how it becomes a rut.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To do again what was done. The root's seeking-again is neutral about outcome: repetition is how a thing becomes a practice, and it is exactly how it becomes a rut.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin repetere (to seek again, to attack again): re- (again) + petere (to seek, to aim at); repetition is a seeking done more than once, and whether it becomes practice or a rut depends entirely on what is sought.

rows.definition: To put one thing where another was. Replacement fills the role and is not the same thing.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To put one thing where another was. The root's space-filling is honest about its limits: replacement fills the role, and it is never the same thing as what it fills it with.
rows.historical_meaning: Re- (Latin, again) attached to place, from Old French place, from Latin platea (a broad street), from Greek plateia (broad way); to replace is to put something into the space another thing once occupied, filling the space rather than restoring the thing.

rows.definition: What takes the place of something removed. A replacement fills the role and is not the same thing.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: What takes the place of something removed. A replacement fills the role and, as the root's own space-filling admits, is not the same thing as what it replaced.
rows.historical_meaning: Built on replace, from Latin platea (a broad way), by way of place; a replacement is what now occupies a space once held by something else, without being that something else.

rows.definition: An answer sent back to whoever asked. A reply closes a turn and opens the next.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: An answer sent back to whoever asked. The root's folding-back closes one turn of a conversation and, by the same motion, opens the next.
rows.historical_meaning: Old French replier, from Latin replicare (to fold back): re- (back) + plicare (to fold); a reply is, at its root, a folding-back of an answer toward whoever first spoke.

rows.definition: Repository shortened to its spoken name — one project's whole history and truth in one place.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Repository shortened to its spoken name — one project's whole history and truth in one place. The root's storing is unbroken by the clipping: everything is still put back into the same place, every time.
rows.historical_meaning: Clipped from repository, from Latin repositorium (a place for storing), from reponere (to put back, to store): re- (back) + ponere (to place); a repo is a single place a whole project's history is put back into and kept.

rows.definition: An account carried back to someone who was not present. A rendering, whose honesty is the whole of its worth.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: An account carried back to someone who was not present. A rendering whose honesty is the whole of its worth, exactly as the root's carrying-back promises nothing but the delivery.
rows.historical_meaning: Old French reporter, from Latin reportare (to carry back): re- (back) + portare (to carry); a report is, at its root, an account physically carried back to someone who was not present to see the thing for themselves.

rows.definition: Request shortened to its parameter name — the asking half of every exchange, as code spells it.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Request shortened to its parameter name. The asking half of every exchange, spelled the way code spells it rather than the way speech does.
rows.historical_meaning: Clipped from request, from Latin requirere (to seek again, to ask for): re- (again) + quaerere (to seek); req shortens the word to its parameter name and keeps none of the asking's grammar, only its function.

rows.definition: An asking that may be refused. A request differs from a demand by leaving the answer open.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: An asking that may be refused. The root's seeking never guaranteed an answer, which is exactly what separates a request from a demand.
rows.historical_meaning: Old French requeste, from Latin requirere/requaerere (to seek again, to ask for): re- (again) + quaerere (to seek, to ask); a request is an asking that leaves room for refusal, unlike a demand, which the root does not.

rows.definition: To make a thing necessary rather than optional. Requirement removes a choice on purpose.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To make a thing necessary rather than optional. The root's insistent seeking becomes a demand, removing a choice on purpose rather than by accident.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin requirere (to seek again, to need): re- (again) + quaerere (to seek); to require is to seek a thing so insistently that it stops being optional.

rows.definition: A thing that must hold for the whole to be acceptable. A requirement removes a choice on purpose.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A thing that must hold for the whole to be acceptable. Like require, its root's seeking has hardened into something no longer negotiable — a requirement removes a choice on purpose.
rows.historical_meaning: Built on require, from Latin requirere (to seek again, to need): re- (again) + quaerere (to seek); a requirement is what the insistent seeking of the root settles on as necessary for the whole to hold.

rows.definition: The careful going-and-looking-again — study that returns with sources, never with guesses.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The careful going-and-looking-again — study that returns with sources, never with guesses. The root's repeated circling is the discipline itself: one look is a glance, and research is what happens after several.
rows.historical_meaning: Old French recerchier: re- (again) + cerchier (to search), from Latin circare (to go around), from circus (a circle); research is, at its root, a careful going-around and back again, not a single pass.

rows.definition: The mail service this house sends through, and the act of sending again. A named tool, and a plain verb.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The mail service this house sends through, and the act of sending again. A named tool and a plain verb sharing one root, both about the same message reaching its destination a second time.
rows.historical_meaning: Re- (Latin, again) attached to send, from Old English sendan, from Proto-Germanic sandijan; to resend is to send the same thing a second time, whether by a hand, a wire, or the mail service that borrows the plain verb as its name.

rows.definition: To return a thing to a known starting state. A reset discards what accumulated, on purpose.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To return a thing to a known starting state. The root's placing is done on purpose here — a reset discards what accumulated, because starting clean was the point.
rows.historical_meaning: Re- (Latin, again) attached to set, from Old English settan (to place, to set), from Proto-Germanic satjan; to reset is to place a thing back at a known starting point, discarding whatever had accumulated since.

rows.definition: That which returns a thing to a known starting state. It discards what accumulated, on purpose.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: That which returns a thing to a known starting state. It discards what accumulated, on purpose, exactly as the root's plain placing always intended.
rows.historical_meaning: An agent noun built on reset, from Old English settan (to place, to set); a resetter is named for the returning-to-place, not for whatever had accumulated before it acted.

rows.definition: What remains and keeps returning after the first exchange is done. A share that continues rather than concludes.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: What remains and keeps returning after the first exchange is done. The root's sitting-behind is a fitting image for a share that continues rather than concludes.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin residuus (remaining, left over), from residere (to remain behind, to settle): re- (back) + sedere (to sit); a residual is what stays sitting after the first exchange has already moved on.

rows.definition: To change how much space a thing takes. Resizing alters the fit and not the thing.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To change how much space a thing takes. Resizing alters the fit and leaves the thing itself untouched, exactly as the root's reassessment only ever changed the measure, never the measured.
rows.historical_meaning: Re- (Latin, again) attached to size, from Old French sise, a clipping of assise (an assessment, a fixed regulation), from Latin assidere (to sit beside, to assess): ad- (to) + sedere (to sit); to resize is to sit down again with a thing's measure and set it differently.

rows.definition: The settling of something unsettled, and how fine a detail a view can show. Both are about how much is finally made clear.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The settling of something unsettled, and how fine a detail a view can show. Both readings share the root's untying: each is about how much is finally made clear from what had been knotted or blurred.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin resolutio (a loosening, an unfastening), from resolvere (to loosen, to untie): re- (again) + solvere (to loosen); resolution is the untying of something knotted, whether that knot is a dispute or a blur too coarse to see through.

rows.definition: To bring an unsettled thing to a settled state. Also to turn a reference into the thing it points at.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To bring an unsettled thing to a settled state, or to turn a reference into the thing it points at. The root's untying covers both: something knotted is loosened until it is plain.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin resolvere (to loosen, to untie, to dissolve): re- (again) + solvere (to loosen); to resolve is to untie an unsettled thing into a settled one, or to untie a reference into the thing it was always pointing at.

rows.definition: Something available to be drawn on. Calling a thing a resource already frames it by its usefulness to someone.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Something available to be drawn on. The root's rising-again is a fair frame: calling a thing a resource already treats it as something kept in reserve for whoever needs it to rise.
rows.historical_meaning: Old French resourdre/ressource, from Latin resurgere (to rise again): re- (again) + surgere (to rise); a resource was first a rising-up-again, a reserve that could be drawn on to recover, before it meant simply anything available to be used.

rows.definition: What comes back when something is asked. A response answers; it does not have to satisfy.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: What comes back when something is asked. The root's pledging is the whole obligation: a response answers, and the root never promised that it would satisfy.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin responsum, from respondere (to answer, to pledge in return): re- (back) + spondere (to pledge, to promise); a response is a pledge sent back to meet a pledge sent first, and the root never required that it satisfy, only that it answer.

rows.definition: Answerable for — the one a duty comes home to; ownership's ethical face.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Answerable for — the one a duty comes home to. The root's pledging is ownership's ethical face: a promise made means someone stays reachable when it is time to answer for it.
rows.historical_meaning: Built on respond, from Latin respondere (to answer, to pledge in return): re- (back) + spondere (to pledge); to be responsible is to be the one a pledge comes home to, answerable when it is called on.

rows.definition: Changing shape to suit the conditions it meets. Accommodation without loss of identity.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Changing shape to suit the conditions it meets. The root's answering is accommodation without surrender — a responsive thing still keeps its own identity while it keeps replying.
rows.historical_meaning: Built on respond, from Latin respondere (to answer): re- (back) + spondere (to pledge); to be responsive is to keep answering back to whatever conditions change, without losing the shape that is answering.

rows.definition: What remains, and the ceasing of effort. In this house the second sense is honoured and never prescribed to another.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: What remains, and the ceasing of effort. The second sense is the one honoured here and never prescribed to anyone else — the root allows both readings, and only one of them is ever a rule for someone else to follow.
rows.historical_meaning: Old English ræst/rest (repose, sleep, a resting place), from Proto-Germanic rastu- (rest, a stopping place); rest has named both what remains and the ceasing of effort for as long as the word is recorded, without either sense crowding out the other.

rows.definition: The bringing back of a thing to a former condition. Restoration returns the form; the interval is never returned.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The bringing back of a thing to a former condition. Restoration returns the form, and the root is silent on the interval — that is never returned along with it.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin restauratio, from restaurare (to restore, to rebuild), from instaurare (to renew, to set up again): in- (upon) + a root related to Greek histanai (to stand); restoration brings back a form, and the root makes no claim about the time that passed while the form was gone.

rows.definition: To bring a thing back to a state it held before. Restoration returns the form and never the interval.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To bring a thing back to a state it held before. Restoration returns the form and never the interval, exactly as the root's standing-up-again says nothing about the time spent down.
rows.historical_meaning: Old French restorer, from Latin restaurare (to restore, to rebuild), from instaurare (to renew): in- (upon) + a root related to Greek histanai (to make to stand); to restore is to set a thing standing again in a state it held before.

rows.definition: To narrow what may be done. Restriction is a choice removed, and should say by whom.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: To narrow what may be done. The root's binding is never anonymous — a restriction drawn tight by nobody in particular should still say by whom it was drawn.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin restringere (to draw back tightly, to bind fast): re- (back) + stringere (to draw tight, to bind); to restrict is to bind something so it cannot move as freely as it once could.

rows.definition: A bound placed on what may be done. Restriction is a choice removed, and it should say by whom.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A bound placed on what may be done. It is a choice removed, and the root's own binding was never self-applied — it should always say by whom.
rows.historical_meaning: Built on restrict, from Latin restringere (to draw back tightly, to bind fast): re- (back) + stringere (to bind); a restriction is a bound placed by the same tightening the root describes.

rows.definition: That which rearranges a whole's parts and their relations. It changes what is possible without changing what is there.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: That which rearranges a whole's parts and their relations. It changes what is possible without changing what is there, in the same way the root's piling can be rebuilt without adding or removing a single stone.
rows.historical_meaning: An agent noun built on restructure, from re- (Latin, again) attached to structure, from Latin structura (a fitting together, a building), from struere (to pile, to build); a restructurer rearranges the piled-together parts without changing what is there.
